The Prophet told young men who can support a wife to marry, or else fast, and rejected companions' vows of celibacy, Uthman b. Maz'un's included, saying he himself marries.
Castration was forbidden and temporary marriage permitted; Jabir says it was practised until Umar forbade it, and another report says it was allowed three nights at Autas, then forbidden.
Sabra contracted a temporary marriage for his cloak in the Year of Victory, then the Prophet forbade it until the Day of Resurrection; Ibn Zubair and Ibn Abbas disputed it.
Ali told Ibn Abbas that on the Day of Khaibar the Prophet forbade temporary marriage forever, along with the flesh of domestic asses.
A woman may not be married together with her paternal or maternal aunt, nor seek her sister's divorce to take her share, nor a man propose over his brother's proposal.
A Muhrim may neither marry, arrange a marriage nor propose, Uthman reports; Ibn Abbas says the Prophet married Maimuna in Ihram, while Maimuna says he was not.
None may propose over his brother's proposal or bargain over his bargain until he gives way, nor a townsman sell for a villager, nor a woman seek her sister's divorce.
The Prophet forbade Shighar, exchanging daughters or sisters in marriage with no dower, and said the conditions most worthy of fulfilment are those that make intercourse lawful.
A previously married woman must be consulted and has more right to herself than her guardian; a virgin's permission is asked, her silence being her consent.
The Prophet told a man marrying an Ansari woman to look at her, and found his dower of four uqiyas too much, sending him on an expedition.
Marrying Umm Salama, the Prophet stayed three nights, offering a week only if every wife got one; a new virgin bride is given seven nights, a previously married one three.
A woman is married for property, status, beauty or religion, so choose religion; asked why not a virgin, Jabir said his previously married wife could care for his sisters.
An Arab woman the Prophet came to propose to sought refuge with Allah from him, not knowing him, and he left her; then Sahl served him drink from a cup.
Aisha said the verse on a wife fearing her husband's aversion concerns a long-married wife he would divorce, who asks him to keep her, permitting him another wife.
